name: Boeing 747
headline: length
subtitle: 747-400 and 747-8
description: The Boeing 747 'jumbo jet' first flew in 1969 and is known for its hump-shaped upper deck. Boeing's airport planning documents give the 747-400 a length of 231 ft 10 in (70.67 m) and the stretched 747-8 a length of 250 ft 2 in (76.25 m), with wingspans of about 64.4 m and 68.4 m. The heaviest 747-8 can take off at 987,000 lb.

measures.label: Wingspan
measures.note: 747-400 (211 ft 5 in, jig position) to 747-8 (224 ft 5 in)

measures.label: Tail height
measures.note: Ground to top of the tail, varying with version, loading and attitude

measures.label: Maximum takeoff weight
measures.note: Lightest listed 747-400 (GE engines) to the 747-8 passenger version

facts.text: The 747-8 is 250 ft 2 in (76.25 m) long with a 224 ft 5 in (68.40 m) wingspan and a maximum takeoff weight of 987,000 lb (447,695 kg).
The 747-400 is 231 ft 10.25 in (70.67 m) long; its maximum takeoff weight ranges from 800,000 to 875,000 lb with General Electric engines.

sources.title: 747-400 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning (D6-58326-1, Rev F, December 2024)
747-8 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning (D6-58326-3, Rev D, December 2024)

caveats: Ranges run from the 747-400 to the 747-8. Earlier versions (747-100 to -300) are not included.
Each range starts with the 747-400 value from Boeing document D6-58326-1 and ends with the 747-8 value from D6-58326-3.
